data.title: Chat: the AS-98 href allowlist guard misses compound assignment (||=, ??=, &&=) on a new anchor

data.body: Filed from the AS-98 QA review (finding F1, agent:qa-priya, 2026-09-11, at head 156faa5); re-filed from AS-119 (cancelled) to carry the Chat set's critical priority. OBSERVED, not argued: a new anchor in app.js doing 'p1.href ||= task.taskId' survives every AS-93/AS-98 guard (link-sites.test.js and the api.test.js link-site tests: 67/67 green). Cause: HREF_ASSIGN only recognises '=' and '+=', and MECHANISMS bans only '.href +=', so '||=' / '??=' / '&&=' are invisible to T8 (allowlist) and T9 (mechanism ban), and the href-assignment count pin never increments. Narrowed by Priya's probe P8: the same operator on an EXISTING site IS red {T7, T8} via the count going 9 -> 8, so only a fresh element evades. Priya judged it not an honest-mistake spelling and deliberately did not apply the fix inline because it changes guard behaviour. Proposed close (one regex): add the compound operators to MECHANISMS (a pattern matching .href followed by ||= or ??= or &&=), or widen HREF_ASSIGN to admit compound operators so the count pin and allowlist both see them; with an anchored mutant re-running P8-on-a-new-anchor and observing red. complexity: low; test-only guard tightening; joins the tail of the Chat-set age queue. Note for the planner: AS-115 (click-to-copy chips, in needs_human at 124440b) adds test/copy-refs.test.js with its own whitespace-insensitive href-assignment count pin over app.js; keep the two pins consistent.

Plan written (0deb7fe). Key call: make the operator set explicit and closed — HREF_ASSIGN admits all 16 ECMAScript assignment operators so a compound op on a NEW anchor is both a tenth assignment (count pin) and a violation (op !== '='); MECHANISMS independently bans every compound op plus Reflect.set( and Object.defineProperty(/defineProperties( as whole bans (zero uses on master, same reasoning as AS-98 §1.5). New T12 drives both regexes with a literal 16-operator array + 5 comparison spellings so the mechanism half is falsifiable (M9). Nine anchored mutants, 8 red / 1 boundary-green (destructuring target, §1.4). Baseline measured on master d2d6608: host 554/553/1 skipped; predicted 555. AS-115's copy-refs T17 pin shares the gap and is not edited here (seam ruling §6). Marcus implements, Priya reviews (§7 says why her filing the finding is not the AS-98 §8 conflict). Branch feat/AS-120-href-assignment-operators, worktree .worktrees/AS-120. Planning stage ran on Opus under the Fable-limit fallback.

Implemented — ready for review at 889a566 on feat/AS-120-href-assignment-operators (2 commits, developer-marcus, no .lattice on the branch). Findings first: (F1) plan AC-2 asks that M3's T8 failure message name the &&= violation, but T8's count assertion fires before its violations assertion, so the message read only 'found 10' — and the violation strings carried rhs without the operator. Fixed in 889a566: violation strings are now '<file>: .href <op> <rhs>' and the count message appends them when present. This touches T8's messages, which plan §2 said were unchanged; deliberate deviation in favour of AC-2, no other T8 change. Observed after the fix: 'found 10; violations: app.js: .href &&= dashHref(task.taskId)'. (F2, informational) M1 against master's test file (0deb7fe) is 67/67 green — the hole observed before the fix, exactly as §3 predicted. What was built (2648089): ASSIGN_OP enumerates the 16 ECMA-262 assignment operators (longest first); HREF_ASSIGN built from it; independent HREF_COMPOUND for the 15 compound forms; MECHANISMS 4->6 ('.href +=' replaced by '.href <compound>=', plus Reflect.set( and Object.defineProperty(/defineProperties( as whole bans); T9 retitled AS-98/AS-120 '...plain .href = assignment'; T11 rejected 9->12 (P8 verbatim, ??= task.url, &&= dashHref(...)); new T12 with a literal 16-string operator array (asserted length 16, not derived from ASSIGN_OP) driving both regexes plus 5 comparison spellings; file header sentence per §1; README sentence per §2. classifyHrefAssignments untouched. Host suite on the branch tip (node --test in apps/chat): baseline at 0deb7fe 554 / 553 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped; at 889a566 555 / 554 / 0 / 1 — plan §5 predicted 555/554/0/1, exact. Mutants: 9 runs + M1-vs-master in a detached /tmp/AS-120-mutant worktree (removed after), host runs of api.test.js + link-sites.test.js (68 tests), applied-assertion per run = MUTANT-M<id> 0->1, git diff --stat exactly one file, A-panel count 1, mutated diff re-read. Observed red sets, all exactly as §3: M1 {T8,T9}; M2 {T8,T9,T10} (T7 green); M3 {T7,T8,T9}; M4 {T8,T9}; M5 {T9} (T8 green, count 9); M6 {T9}; M7 all green (boundary, by design); M8 {T11,T12}; M9 {T12}. 8 red, 1 green-by-design, 0 survivors. Runner and logs in scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-120/. Not done, by the orchestrator's instruction: compose --build receipts (baseline and per-mutant -p asc-as120-*) — docker is off PATH in this lane and AC-6/AC-8 name the reviewer's runs; Priya takes them. Cleanup: $W git diff --exit-code clean, worktree list = master + AS-106 + AS-115 + AS-120, no /tmp/AS-120-*, no images created.

REVIEW (agent:qa-priya, on Opus under the Fable fallback; tick watcher:26252 loop tick 18, resumed from the cut-off lane in tick 17). Branch feat/AS-120-href-assignment-operators at 889a566 (2 commits, both developer-marcus <developer-marcus@agents.american-software.local>), diff master...branch = apps/chat/README.md (+3/-1) and apps/chat/test/link-sites.test.js (+78/-18); no .lattice/ on the branch; merge-tree clean vs master 430a35c and vs feat/AS-115-copy-refs. VERDICT: PASS. No inline fixes made. Marcus's implemented comment was read only after my own results were formed; no daemon note was read.

FINDINGS FIRST (M5). Blocking: 0. Outside the criteria list: 2, both non-blocking, filed as AS-123 (backlog, tag chat, low). F1 — quote class: the setAttribute('href' and ['href'] mechanism regexes admit only ' and \", so open[`href`] = x and open.setAttribute(`href`, x) are count 0 / no mechanism hit (T8 blind, T9 blind). Not an honest-mistake idiom; not a stated criterion of this plan or AS-98 (whose English names the quoted spellings literally) — boundary, backlog. F2 — RHS swallow: [^;\n]* captures to end of statement, so a second .href assignment in the same statement after an allowlisted first one is invisible: a.href = dashHref(x), b.href = task.taskId; and cond ? (a.href = dashHref(x)) : (b.href = task.taskId); both classify count 1 / zero violations. Adversarial-leaning (not house style), backlog. One plan deviation, judged and accepted: 889a566 changes T8's count-assertion message to append the violations, against plan §2 'T8 messages unchanged' — but the plan's own AC-2 requires M3's T8 message to name the &&= violation, and with the count assertion firing first that is impossible without the change; message-only, no behaviour change; my M3 receipt shows 'violations: app.js: .href &&= dashHref(task.taskId)'. Concur with the implementer's choice.

M6 PROBES PAST THE LIST (27 inputs, host, classifier and MECHANISMS extracted verbatim from the branch file by scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-120/probe.mjs). Red as expected (T8 violation): newline between .href and =, open.href = open.href || dashHref(), ternary RHS, pv.href ?? x, chained a.href = b.href = dashHref(), parenthesised RHS, new URL(...).href, location.href = x, .href=x no-space, ||= with tabs, >>>=, **=, dashHref chained after a newline dot. Red T9 only: Object.defineProperties (definePropert(?:y|ies) covers it), Object.assign. Green by AS-98's stated English ('begins with'): open.href = dashHref(x) + '#top' — allowed, by design, recorded not filed. Blind, adversarial, confirming the §1.4 lexical boundary: a.href /* */ = x, a . href = x, createAttribute('href') + setAttributeNode. Blind, filed (F1/F2 above). Correct negatives: a.hreflang = x count 0; comparisons count 0. Benign false positive: a.dataset.href = x counts (safe direction). T12's operator array confirmed literal (16 strings, length asserted), not derived from ASSIGN_OP. app.js:298 permalink classifies as serializeChatUrl( under the new regex; all 9 sites on the branch are op '=' (app.js:160,177,205,264,298,457,718,800,964), 12 files, total 9. HTML sinks (innerHTML etc.) are already banned by api.test.js purity guards — not a gap here.

COUNTS (cardinality first). Host branch 889a566: 37 files, 555 tests / 554 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped, exit 0. Host master 8b32a37: 562 / 561 / 0 / 1 (master moved +7 since the plan's 554 via AS-102; merge base 0deb7fe; branch is +1 over its base as §5 predicts). Compose --build from $W, project asc-review-as120-final: 'Image asc-review-as120-final-test Built', 555 / 548 / 0 fail / 7 skipped, exit 0 — AC-6 exact. Master-test-file compose (M1master, mutant tree with master's link-sites.test.js): 'Image asc-review-as120-m1master-test Built', 554 / 547 / 0 / 7 — AC-1's all-green half.

MUTANTS (AC-8: 9 named + M7b + M1master = 11 runs, each compose --build with its own project, Built line present in every log, applied-assertion recorded per run — marker x1 at the intended line, diff-stat one file (two for M1master), A-panel intact for insertions). Scratch copy: detached worktree .worktrees/AS-120-mutant at 889a566, never $W. Red sets EXACT to plan §3 in all cases, 0 survivors: M1 {T8,T9} (message names .href ||= task.taskId; count 10); M2 {T8,T9,T10} (T7 green as predicted); M3 {T7,T8,T9} (T7 5->6; T8 names &&=); M4 {T8,T9} (-= 1); M5 {T9} only, T8 green at 9 (why the mechanism ban exists); M6 {T9} only; M7 all GREEN by design (§1.4 boundary observed); M7b (same destructuring on the existing A-panel site) {T7,T8} — T7 'task panel goes through dashHref()', T8 found 8 — AC-5's second half; M8 (ASSIGN_OP restored to \+?=) {T11,T12}; M9 (HREF_COMPOUND restored to \.href\s*\+=) {T12} only, message names 'x.href *= y;'. Tally 11 runs: 9 red exactly as predicted, 2 green exactly as predicted (M7, M1master). Note on my own tooling: M8/M9 first reported NOT APPLIED because my assertion expected the app.js A-panel line to vanish for any replacement; the mutations had applied at the intended lines (test file :36 and :43) — assertion corrected to app.js-only, re-run, results above. Logs: scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-120/asc-review-as120-*.log (M1-M4 from tick 17, identified by their violation messages; the rest from this tick), mutant-summary.txt.

FLOOR CHECK (AC sweep, second, labelled as such): AC-1 pass (M1 red {T8,T9} on branch, all-green with master's test file, both Built). AC-2 pass (M2/M3/M4 exact; M3 message names &&=). AC-3 pass (M5, M6 each {T9} only). AC-4 pass (T12 green; T11 at 12 rejected / 5 accepted — read in diff; M8 {T11,T12}, M9 {T12}). AC-5 pass (M7 green; M7b {T7,T8}). AC-6 pass (555/554/0/1 host; 555/548/0/7 compose, Built line quoted). AC-7 pass (README sentence matches §2 verbatim; file header carries the §1 English). AC-8 pass (11 runs, all applied-assertions recorded). AC-9 pass (no as120 images after teardown; my scratch worktree was .worktrees/AS-120-mutant, not /tmp, removed; worktree list = master + AS-106/108/115/120; $W clean, git diff --exit-code). 9 of 9 pass, with 2 findings outside the list (above). Open question §8 Q2 (T7a's .url operator blindness): closes as default 'leave it' — M2 shows T10 catching the .url read regardless of operator; no surviving .url path found.

HYGIENE. docker network ls before: 18 networks incl. asc-review-as120_default leaked from my cut-off tick-17 lane; after: 17 — that one removed by down -v --rmi local --remove-orphans, every per-mutant project torn down inside its run (leftover check none for each), nothing else touched. Pre-existing leaked networks from earlier tasks (asc-as93-*, asc-as94-lena, asc-as95-qa-*, asc-chat-qa23, asc-marcus95) are not mine and were left alone (AS-106's problem). Unfinished: nothing from the plan; the only cut is that M6 probes ran on the host classifier rather than inside compose (the compose runs cover T8/T12 on the real tree, as §4 asks). Status unchanged — orchestrator moves to done.
